subtitle: Lesson 22 · Post-Exploitation and Privilege Escalation

eyebrow: A misconfiguration review, not a trick

steps.label: Weak service permissions
steps.sub: a LocalSystem service with a writable binary path or registry key

steps.label: Unquoted service paths
steps.sub: a path-parsing ambiguity that can run a file from a writable location

steps.label: AlwaysInstallElevated
steps.sub: a policy letting any user install software with SYSTEM privileges

steps.label: Stored credentials
steps.sub: secrets left in scheduled tasks or unattended-install files

eyebrow: The same audit discipline, on Linux

steps.label: SUID / SGID binaries
steps.sub: an unusual binary running with its owner's privileges, not the caller's

steps.label: Sudoers misconfigurations
steps.sub: a NOPASSWD entry broad enough to read or write arbitrary files

steps.label: World-writable cron jobs
steps.sub: a root-run script anyone can edit

steps.label: Kernel / capability gaps
steps.sub: an unpatched local-escalation CVE or over-granted capability

code:
# These are CIS Benchmark / hardening-audit categories,
# the same ones course 8 already teaches defenders to check:
#
#  - service ACLs and registry policy
#  - SUID/SGID file permissions
#  - sudoers and cron file permissions
#  - kernel patch level and granted capabilities
caption: A pentest proves these are unremediated — it doesn't invent the risk category.
